Argentina.name: Lionel Messi
Argentina.tactical: Primary Playmaker. Drops deep into the right half-space to dictate tempo. Often operates as a False 9, requiring runners in behind to exploit space created by his gravity.

Argentina.name: Emiliano Martínez
Argentina.tactical: Sweeper Keeper. Elite shot-stopper with an aggressive box presence. Unparalleled psychological dominance during penalty shootouts.

Argentina.name: Julián Álvarez
Argentina.tactical: Relentless Pressing Forward. His high work rate off the ball makes him the perfect foil for Messi. Excels at finding pockets of space in congested boxes.

France.name: Kylian Mbappé
France.tactical: Inside Forward. Utilizes explosive pace to break lines. Primarily operates in the left channel, cutting inside to shoot. Requires a target man to play off of.

France.name: Antoine Griezmann
France.tactical: Advanced Playmaker / Box-to-Box. The tactical engine. Has evolved into a hybrid 8/10 who dictates play, switches the ball effortlessly, and provides elite defensive cover.

France.name: William Saliba
France.tactical: Ball-Playing Defender. Anchors the high line. Elite recovery pace and exceptional composure on the ball to build out from the back under severe pressing.
achievements: Premier League PFA Team of the Year

USA.name: Christian Pulisic
USA.tactical: Direct Winger. The focal point of the USMNT transition attack. Uses low center of gravity to carry the ball vertically and commit defenders in the final third.

USA.name: Weston McKennie
USA.tactical: Box-to-Box Midfielder. High-volume ball winner with an elite aerial presence on set pieces. Crucial for disrupting opposition build-up play.

USA.name: Antonee Robinson
USA.tactical: Attacking Fullback. Provides the primary width on the left flank, allowing the winger to invert. Elite stamina allows him to recover rapidly in defensive transitions.

Brazil.name: Vinícius Júnior
Brazil.tactical: Inverted Winger. Arguably the most lethal 1v1 dribbler in the world. Thrives in isolation on the left wing before driving to the byline or cutting across the box.

Brazil.name: Rodrygo
Brazil.tactical: Versatile Forward. Elite close-quarters combination play. Often drifts centrally to overload the penalty area and link up with the center forward.

Brazil.name: Bruno Guimarães
Brazil.tactical: Deep-Lying Destroyer. Combines South American flair in tight spaces with Premier League physicality. The crucial pivot connecting the defense to the attack.

England.name: Jude Bellingham
England.tactical: Shadow Striker / Number 10. Makes devastating late runs into the penalty area. Unmatched physical presence allows him to dominate aerial duels and physical pressing traps.

England.name: Harry Kane
England.tactical: Complete Forward. Elite finishing combined with the passing range of a playmaker. Drops deep to pull center-backs out of position, creating space for wingers to exploit.

England.name: Declan Rice
England.tactical: Single Pivot. Covers massive ground horizontally to protect the back four. Excellent at carrying the ball out of pressure to break the first line of defense.
